thread:
jordan: Quick debugging dump for the TP all-reduce cliff we saw on the 8xTP runs.
jordan: Short summary: p99 spikes when per-rank message sizes cross ~96KB-140KB. Ring path latency jumps; tree fallback sometimes helps but throughput drops.
jordan: Setup: 4x nodes, 8-way TP (so 32 ranks total), A100-80GB, NVLink. NCCL 2.14, CUDA 12.1, driver 535.86.
jordan: Microbench results (single-step all-reduce on 32 ranks):
```
msg_size  p50(ms)  p99(ms)
8KB      1.8      2.6
48KB     2.5      3.8
96KB     3.1      7.9   <- cliff
128KB    3.6      12.3  <- big jump
256KB    5.4      14.8
```
jordan: I profiled with nvtx + perf counters and saw long stalls during NCCL rendezvous/chop and a burst of kernel launches that serialize on the stream.
maya: Did you see KV cache flushes interleaving? that can create unpredictable msg boundaries.
jordan: Yes — kvcache flushes occur every 32k on our workload due to prefix mismatches, so many all-reduce ops are coming in as fragmented submessages. nvprof shows many small transfers then a larger final chunk.
sam: Fragmentation + NCCL algorithm switch could explain it. NCCL switches algo based on msg size ranges; the switch boundary around 96-128KB fits.
sam: Also check NCCL_COLL_NET_PROTOCOL and NCCL_TREE_THRESHOLD envs.
jordan: I ran a control where I forced NCCL to ring-only vs tree-only via envs. Ring-only: slightly better p50 for small msgs but much worse p99 at cliff. Tree-only: helps p99 across the cliff but compute overlap suffers and CPU-side serialization rose.

jordan: Key oddity: kernel selector in runtime schedules a final reduce kernel that waits for all partial recv callbacks; if partials are many (due to fragmentation) we get more kernel launch bursts that saturate GPU driver queue and block other compute kernels.
tasha: That sounds like a scheduling knob — can we change the kernel-launch strategy to batch small reduce kernels into a single fused kernel when fragmentation count > N?
jordan: I prototyped a naive fuse at runtime: coalesce reduce ops within a 1ms window into a single kernel. p99 drops from 12.3ms -> 8.1ms for 128KB case but p50 slightly worsens. tradeoff seems okay for tail-sensitive loads.

maya: Nice. Any non-invasive experiments? e.g., change rendezvous chunking threshold so NCCL sees larger logical msg and picks tree earlier.
jordan: I tried bumping `RNDV_CHUNK_BYTES` from 64KB -> 192KB in our local NCCL build (or equivalent RT env). That moved the algorithm selection earlier; p99 improved to ~9.0ms but we lost some overlap on live workloads.
sam: Can you share the nvprof flamegraph link? want to see overlap lines.
jordan: Uploaded: https://perf.internal/redwood/flames/2523456789
maya: Looking — you can see a train of tiny cudaMemcpyAsync entries before ncclAllReduce kicks in. Those tiny copies are kvcache small misses.

infra-bot: perf-ci/job/3421 finished: regression detected on allreduce p99 +12% for commit b7c2d3; job log: https://ci.redwood/jobs/3421
jordan: That regression timeline matches when we changed batching heuristics (we reduced microbatch coalescing to save memory). Reverting that change brings p99 back down.
tasha: For a long-term fix we should consider three mitigations:
- runtime: kernel-fusion heuristic when fragmentation_count > X
- routing: prefer tree-reduce for mid-sized logical msgs when pipeline degree > 4
- kvcache: align/round buffers to avoid tiny flushes (coalesce before sending)

sam: Agreed. Also add a perf test in CI that microbench all-reduce across the same TP configs (vary msg sizes 8K..512K) and assert p99 thresholds.
jordan: I'll send a small PR with:
```
- runtime: add coalescing window (opt-in via ENV: RW_COALESCE_WINDOW_MS)
- kvcache: optional align_to param (defaults off)
- ci: microbench job + perf baseline
```
jordan: Anyone want to pair on the perf CI test? need help plumbing the perf collector and storing artifacts.
maya: I can take the CI collector part.
tasha: I'll own the runtime kernel-fuse sketch. sam can own kvcache alignment.

jordan: Final note: beware of pushing naive tree-only defaults — in many runs tree reduces concurrency and hurts throughput. we need workload-aware routing.
maya: Agreed — add a gate: only prefer tree if (logical_msg_size in [96KB,512KB]) && (tp_degree >= 6) && (kvcache_fragment_count > threshold).

jordan: Thanks all — I'll open the three PRs and link here. short followup planned after CI runs.
maya: :thumbsup:
sam: nice work.
